papers.title: EnvHarness: Awakening Static Worlds for Agent Learning
papers.what: Wraps a static agent environment in programmable plug-in components that reshape its behaviour while keeping the original verifier intact, with a companion system that reads the policy's own failure trajectories to decide what to reshape, giving up to a 9.0-point gain on held-out instances with 9.8% fewer execution steps across five benchmarks in four domains.
papers.builds_on: ADaPT (2023, J8DYBKW2); LATS (2024, 77ERE7HA); Offline RL Tutorial (2020, ZULLM3UF)

papers.title: SPADE: Self-Play in Adaptive Synthetic Executable Environments
papers.what: Lets one language model write its own executable Gym-style training environments as Environment Designer and learn to solve them as Reasoning Agent, aiming the Designer with a regret signal measured as the reward gap with and without privileged hints, for +5.3 over the strongest fixed-environment baseline at 30B and +13.9 on ACEBench-Agent.
papers.builds_on: LATS (2024, 77ERE7HA); Offline RL Tutorial (2020, ZULLM3UF); Cross-Entropy Method (2020, ZNEMGMWY)

papers.title: MemTrapBench: Benchmarking Cognitive Traps in LLM Memory Use
papers.what: Shows that faithfully recorded, semantically relevant memories still degrade current-task performance through Reasoning Fixation and Belief Distortion, with all five memory frameworks tested scoring below the no-memory baseline and the strongest still losing more than 10%.
papers.builds_on: Memory Mechanisms Survey (2026, BDY3HUCV); Machine Theory of Mind (2018, NEKX3K3N)

papers.title: Co-RL: Unsupervised Reasoning Emerges from Diverse Cohort in Multi-agent RL
papers.authors: Yang, Bian et al. (UC San Diego)
papers.what: Trains several parameter-decoupled models at once with rewards derived from peers instead of ground-truth labels, using cohort diversity across model families and sizes to decorrelate the errors that cause self-rewarding RL to collapse, for label-free gains of 3.0-8.6% on seven text benchmarks and 2.3-7.2% on four multimodal ones.
